input.rationale: Resolve the open question recorded as a limitation of the previous interpretation: whether the 'leadership transfer in progress' error seen on an explicit transfer to a demoted member belongs to the request itself or to a transfer that was already running when it arrived. This harness runs the same demote-then-transfer setup twice, samples the leader's leadership-transfer flag before the call, immediately after the call returns its future, after the future completes and after a short settle, and issues exactly one request in the first case and the earlier five-attempt sequence in the second while sampling the flag before every attempt. If the flag is clear before the first request and the future still reports an in-progress error, that error belongs to the request; if the flag is already set, the earlier receipt's error is explained by a prior transfer and the target was never attempted.

scope.description: Two cases on separate four-member clusters with one demoted follower each: a single explicit transfer to the demoted member with the leader's transfer flag sampled around the call, and the five-attempt retry sequence with the flag sampled before every attempt.
assumptions: The demoted member is a follower at demotion time, chosen as any member other than the sitting leader.
Each case bootstraps its own cluster, so the two cases share no state.
The harness waits up to two seconds for the demoted member's own GetConfiguration to report the non-voter role and records whether it converged.
The transfer flag is read through the package-internal accessor on the node that is leader at the moment of the call, so the sample describes the node the request is sent to.
excluded: No assertion about client-write availability after the transfer; that was measured in the previous receipt.
Only explicit transfers are issued; the automatic form is covered by the earlier control.
Leadership is sampled every ten milliseconds from each member's State, so a shorter leaderless interval can be missed.

experiment.prefix: Each case bootstraps a four-peer in-memory cluster, waits for a leader, demotes a non-leader member with DemoteVoter, and polls that member's GetConfiguration until it reports the non-voter role. A case event records the demoted member, its role view, convergence time and the leader before the transfer. The single case samples getLeadershipTransferInProgress on the leader, calls LeadershipTransferToServer once, samples the flag again as soon as the future is returned, awaits the future for at most five seconds, samples the flag after completion and again after three hundred milliseconds. The retry case reproduces the five-attempt loop, sampling the flag before each attempt and recording each attempt's error, retrying only while the error names a transfer already in progress. Both result events record the future outcome, the flag samples, whether the named member ever reported Leader during a three-second sample, the leaderless sample count and the final leader.
experiment.responsibility: LeadershipTransferToServer accepts a caller-named member and is documented as transferring leadership to that server; the library owns both the target check and the bookkeeping that decides whether a transfer is already running. An in-progress error returned for a request that was issued while no transfer was running would attribute the failure to that request, while one returned because an earlier transfer was still active would mean the named target was never attempted at all.

comparisons.description: A single explicit transfer to a configured member must install that member if it is accepted; a false witness contradicts it.

The first request must be issued while no transfer is running, so that any in-progress error belongs to that request rather than to an earlier one; a true witness would instead explain the earlier receipt as a prior stalled transfer.

knowledge.assertion: An explicit transfer target is resolved only through leaderState.replState, which includes non-voters, while pickServer skips non-voters.
A voter adopts a higher term and steps down before rejecting a configured non-voter candidate, and timeoutNow forces candidacy without checking suffrage or term.

scope.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters. In both, a non-leader member is chosen as the explicit target; in the trigger case that member is first demoted to non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API and the committed configuration is allowed to reach it, while the control keeps it a voter. Each case records the transfer future's outcome, whether the named target ever reported Leader, whether the final leader is the target, a sampled leaderless interval and the members' terms after the attempt.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms), so a new election can complete quickly.
The demotion is committed before the transfer is requested; the harness waits 200 ms and does not assert configuration convergence separately.

The leaderless interval is estimated from repeated 10 ms sampling whose measured effective rate was about one sample per 116 ms (43 samples), so a shorter leaderless gap can be missed and a zero count is not evidence of absence.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about the effect on client requests accepted during the transfer window, and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely (rejected earlier by the replState lookup) are not exercised.

basis.prefix: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), and selects the first non-leader raft as the target. The trigger calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and sleeps 200 ms; the control skips demotion. The case event records the target role, its term before, and the watch parameters. The harness then calls leader.LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, target.localAddr) and records the future's error and duration, samples target.State() and c.Leader() every 10 ms for the watch window, and emits a result event with future_ok, future_error, future_ms, target_ever_leader, final_leader_is_target, no_leader_ms_sampled, samples, target_term_after and other_member_term_max_after.
basis.responsibility: The library documents that a leadership transfer makes the target up to date, sends TimeoutNow, and that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. Choosing which targets are admissible, and reporting an outcome that matches what happened to authority, are therefore library responsibilities: the caller supplies a member id that the configuration itself currently marks as a non-voter.

A transfer to a member the configuration marks as a non-voter cannot be promoted, so the documented graceful failure requires an error; a successful future contradicts it.

scope.description: One follower of a three-voter configuration is driven through real AppendEntries RPCs on its transport while a single heartbeat is executed on a separate goroutine, as the fast-path contract permits. A stable store holds the heartbeat's term write until the main thread has persisted the newer term; the run records the persisted term sequence, the node's current term before and after, and the log and FSM contents at the affected indexes after a stale-leader request.
assumptions: The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered processHeartbeat handler on a separate goroutine, which is what NetworkTransport's connection handler does; the in-memory transport ignores the registration, so the transport's own dispatch is not exercised.
The stable store delays, but never corrupts or fails, one currentTerm write, modelling a slow store write that completes after a newer term has been persisted.

The term 2 and term 4 AppendEntries requests are supplied by the harness to represent a leader that has committed those indexes elsewhere; their commit indexes are asserted by the request, not produced by a quorum of real nodes.
Election and lease timeouts are raised to 30 s so the follower does not campaign during the sequence.
excluded: No attempt to measure how often the interleaving occurs in a real deployment; the probe only establishes that the interleaving is reachable when a store write is delayed.
No real partition or multi-node cluster is used, and the stale leader's authority is modelled by crafted requests.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 blocks one chosen currentTerm value, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. It first commits entries 2 and 3 at term 2 through trans.AppendEntries on the real consumer path, then installs the blocking hook for term 3 and starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying term 3. Once the hook reports that the term 3 write is in flight, the harness sends a term 4 AppendEntries with entry 4 and leader commit 4 through the transport, waits for it to apply, then releases the term 3 write. It records the current term before and after the release, the persisted term and the sequence of term writes, and finally sends the stale term 3 leader's AppendEntries carrying conflicting entries 4 and 5 with leader commit 5, recording whether that request was accepted, the log payloads at indexes 4 and 5, the FSM payloads at those indexes, the applied and commit indexes, and whether the applied payload at index 4 differs from the log payload there.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease and its applied log prefix never to be replaced. The library owns both: it persists the term, it decides when to raise it, and it performs the truncation that can remove an entry. A transport contract that permits concurrent heartbeat delivery does not relax those duties, so the library must make the term update safe against the concurrency it authorises.

comparisons.description: The persisted current term must not fall below a term the node already adopted; a true value contradicts it.
After the regression, the stale leader's conflicting entries must not replace an entry already applied at a higher term; a true value contradicts it.

scope.description: Two hundred attempts per case on a single follower of a three-voter configuration. Each attempt reads the node's current term, starts a fast-path heartbeat carrying that term plus one on its own goroutine, concurrently sends an AppendEntries carrying the term plus two (with one entry and a matching previous-log index) through the real consumer path, waits for both, and counts the attempt as an inversion when the node's term afterwards is below the higher request's term. The first case leaves the stable store undelayed; the second adds a uniform 0-2 ms delay to every current-term write.
assumptions: One node runs; the two peers are addresses only, so each attempt's higher-term request is a supplied leader message rather than a real election outcome.
The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered handler on its own goroutine, matching the classification and direct invocation that NetworkTransport performs for this request shape.
The undelayed case is not a control for absence of the defect; it measures how often the race occurs when the store adds no latency of its own.
Attempts run sequentially on the same node and reuse its log; terms advance across attempts and are re-read each time.
excluded: No consequence measurement here: this execution only counts term inversions; the truncation consequence was measured separately in the forced-ordering execution.
No multi-node cluster, no real transport framing and no concurrent client load.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 optionally sleeps a uniformly random interval up to a configured maximum before persisting the current term, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. For each attempt it reads r.CurrentTerm() and r.LastIndex(), starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying current+1, sends an AppendEntries carrying current+2, the last log index as PrevLogEntry with its stored term, one entry at the next index and leader commit at that index, then waits for both to finish and records whether the current term is below current+2. Each case emits a case event with the attempt count and maximum delay and a result event with the inversion count.

The library owns the term update and it authorises concurrent heartbeat execution through the transport contract, so the update must remain correct under the concurrency it permits regardless of how the store is timed.

comparisons.description: With no added store delay, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.
With 0-2 ms write jitter, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.

scope.description: Five real nodes over fully connected in-memory transports, bootstrapped from one configuration containing voters A, B and C and non-voters D and E. All nodes share a one-second heartbeat and leader lease; the voters' election timeouts are staggered (A 1.1 s, B 2 s, C and the non-voters 3 s) so that after a partition the two remaining voters do not campaign in lockstep and split the vote. The leader commits 'v1' through a recording FSM, is then disconnected from the other two voters in both directions, and keeps the non-voters reachable in the trigger and loses them in the control. Immediately after the cut the old leader is asked to verify itself; then the harness waits up to twelve seconds for one of the other voters to lead, applies 'v2' there, and asks the old leader to verify itself again before reading its state machine.
assumptions: A caller that verifies the leader before answering a read is the harm model: the experiment measures whether the verification can succeed after the cluster has a different leader.
The injected partition is a bidirectional route removal on the in-memory transports; both sides keep running.
The old leader's lease, not the harness, decides when it stops being leader; the harness only records how that timing compares with the election of a successor.
Both FSM values are read after the successor has applied 'v2', so a value difference means the two state machines disagreed at that moment.
excluded: No restart, no snapshot and no client read protocol; the read is the FSM value a caller would have served.
No asymmetric or intermittent partition, and no disk-backed store.

basis.prefix: The harness creates five in-memory transports and connects every pair in both directions, bootstraps the same configuration (voters A, B, C; non-voters D, E) on all five stores, and starts five rafts each with its own recording FSM. It waits up to ten seconds for a leader, applies 'v1' with a three-second timeout, and sleeps 300 ms so the value is applied everywhere. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the other voters' addresses and theirs from the leader's, and in the control case does the same for the non-voters. It emits sr_case_<case> with the leader identity, the reachable voter and non-voter counts, the initial value and the leader's FSM value, records the cut time, calls VerifyLeader with a two-second bound and records whether it completed, whether it succeeded, its error and the milliseconds since the cut. It waits up to twelve seconds for a voter other than the old leader to report Leader, applies 'v2' there with a three-second timeout, sleeps 300 ms, and records the successor's identity, apply result, FSM value and the milliseconds since the cut. It then calls VerifyLeader on the old leader again with a two-second bound and reads the old leader's FSM value before healing the partition. It emits sr_result_<case> with all of those fields plus stale_verified_read, which is true only when the post-failover verification succeeded and the old leader's value differs from the successor's committed value.
basis.responsibility: VerifyLeader is the licence a caller uses before serving a local read: success tells the caller this node is still the leader that a fresh read requires. The experiment measures whether that window exists in practice and how it compares with the time a successor needs.

A verified read served by the old leader after the successor's commit would be stale data; the harness records whether that combination occurred.

scope.description: One node with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and MaxAppendEntries set to 1, started from an in-memory commit-tracking log store seeded with either exactly 128 command entries or 129, with the staged commit index equal to the seeded entry count and no snapshot. A constructor that has not returned within the observation window is treated as having made no progress, which is what the harness measures rather than assumes.
excluded: No real cluster, no snapshot and no configuration entry in the replayed range.
Only MaxAppendEntries=1; the batch sizes 64 and 1024 were measured by earlier receipts.
No attempt to shut down a node whose constructor never returned.

basis.prefix: The harness seeds an InmemCommitTrackingStore with N command entries at term 1, stages the commit index to N, and starts one raft with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and MaxAppendEntries=1, whose local id is node1 and whose timeouts are 50 ms. A constructor that blocks because it produced into a channel whose only consumer it has not started yet cannot do either: the caller never receives the node, so the caller has no way to start, serve or shut it down. scope.description: One follower node in a three-voter configuration that no live peer drives, with a stable store that optionally sleeps for a uniform random interval before persisting the current term. For each of five delay settings the harness runs 200 attempts; each attempt issues one fast-path heartbeat carrying cur+1 on its own goroutine while a term cur+2 AppendEntries with one entry goes through the real consumer path, then waits for both and records whether the node's current term ended below cur+2. assumptions: The heartbeat shape used here is the one NetworkTransport classifies as a fast path: non-zero term, a leader address, zero previous-log fields, no entries and zero leader commit index.
The delay is applied only to the current-term key, so other stable writes are unaffected and the comparison isolates the term write.
The term cur+2 request reaches the node through the transport's consumer path, which is how a non-heartbeat AppendEntries arrives.
An attempt counts as an inversion when the node's term after both operations is below the higher term it was sent.
excluded: No real leader, partition or quorum; the requests are crafted and their commit indexes are asserted by the request.
No disk-backed store: the delay is a sleep before an in-memory write.

basis.prefix: For each case the harness creates a fresh in-memory stable store wrapped so that a write to the current-term key sleeps for a uniform random duration below the case's maximum, a fresh in-memory transport, and one raft with 30 s timeouts, three voters (the local node plus two addresses with no process) and the option defaults. It bootstraps the configuration, then repeats the attempt 200 times: read the current term and last index, start the fast-path heartbeat on a goroutine through processHeartbeat with a term one above current, build a term-two-above AppendEntries carrying one entry at the last index and a matching previous-log term, send it through the transport, wait for the heartbeat, and count an inversion when the node's term afterwards is below the higher term. Between attempts it sleeps one millisecond. Each case emits sw_case_<case> with the attempt count and the maximum delay in microseconds, and sw_result_<case> with the same fields plus inversion_count.
basis.responsibility: The library permits the registered heartbeat handler to run concurrently with the main AppendEntries path, and it advertises that concurrency as a way to avoid inflating election timeouts for disk latency. The term update must therefore remain monotonic across that overlap, not only when the stable store is instantaneous; the sweep measures how much store latency the current code tolerates before the race saturates.

comparisons.description: With no added delay, the same race must not leave the node below the higher term in any attempt.
A maximum current-term delay of 250 us must not be enough to lose the race.
A maximum current-term delay of 500 us must not be enough to lose the race.
A maximum current-term delay of 1 ms must not be enough to lose the race.
A maximum current-term delay of 2 ms must not be enough to lose the race; this is the setting the earlier two-point probe used.

scope.description: Four real members over the cluster helper's in-memory transports, bootstrapped from one four-voter configuration; one non-leader member is demoted with DemoteVoter and the harness waits until that member's own configuration view no longer lists it as a voter. The leader is then disconnected in both directions from the two other voters and, in the trigger, left connected to the single non-voter; the control also disconnects the non-voter. assumptions: Bidirectional route removal on the in-memory transports models a partition; no process is stopped.
The demoted member's own view is the check that the configuration change reached the node whose acknowledgement is being counted.
A verification that has not completed within two seconds is recorded as incomplete rather than as a success or failure.
excluded: No client read and no second suffrage shape beyond one non-voter.
No demotion of the sitting leader and no cluster larger than four members.

basis.prefix: The harness bootstraps four voters, picks the leader and the three other members, demotes the first non-leader member, and polls that member's GetConfiguration until it no longer reports itself as a voter or two seconds pass, recording whether it converged and after how long. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the other two voters' addresses and theirs from the leader's, and in the control case does the same for the non-voter. It emits vx_case_<case> with the membership counts, the reachable counts, the voter quorum and the demotion convergence, calls VerifyLeader with a two-second bound, and emits vx_result_<case> with whether the call completed, whether it succeeded, its error, the elapsed milliseconds and the node's state afterwards.
basis.responsibility: VerifyLeader sizes its quorum from the voter count, so a leader that can reach only itself among the voters has one of the two acknowledgements its own sizing requires. The experiment asks whether a single non-voter, rather than a particular larger suffrage mix, is enough to supply the missing acknowledgement and let the call report success.

comparisons.description: With one of three voters reachable, a verification sized on the voter quorum must fail; the harness records whether a single non-voter changes that.

semantic_changes: The transfer is issued concurrently with the demotion instead of after it converges.

scope.description: Twenty independent attempts, each on a fresh four-voter in-memory cluster. Per attempt the harness picks the leader and one follower, starts DemoteVoter for that follower on a goroutine, then immediately calls LeadershipTransferToServer for the same member on whichever node is leader at that moment, both with bounded waits. It records whether each future succeeded, whether the target ever reported Leader during the following two seconds, which member led at the end, and the target's own suffrage at the end.
assumptions: Starting the demotion and issuing the transfer without an intervening wait is the tightest race the public API allows; the caller cannot observe commit state between the two calls without waiting.
The target is chosen at demotion time from the members that are not leading, so the demotion never targets the sitting leader.
An attempt in which the target reports Leader at any sample counts as an elevation even if it later steps down.
excluded: No repeated demotions on one cluster; a fresh cluster is built per attempt because a member can be demoted only once.
No partition, no restart, and no client traffic during the race.

before.description: Two leadership-transfer invocations on real four-voter in-memory clusters. In both, a non-leader member is chosen as the explicit target; in the trigger case that member is first demoted to non-voter through the public DemoteVoter API and the committed configuration is allowed to reach it, while the control keeps it a voter. Each case records the transfer future's outcome, whether the named target ever reported Leader, whether the final leader is the target, a sampled leaderless interval and the members' terms after the attempt.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with inmemConfig timeouts (Heartbeat/Election/Lease 50 ms), so a new election can complete quickly.
The demotion is committed before the transfer is requested; the harness waits 200 ms and does not assert configuration convergence separately.

The leaderless interval is estimated from repeated 10 ms sampling whose measured effective rate was about one sample per 116 ms (43 samples), so a shorter leaderless gap can be missed and a zero count is not evidence of absence.
Both cases run in one execution; each builds and closes its own cluster.
excluded: No claim about the effect on client requests accepted during the transfer window, and no safety claim about committed entries.
Transfers to members absent from the configuration entirely (rejected earlier by the replState lookup) are not exercised.

prefix.before: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), and selects the first non-leader raft as the target. The trigger calls leader.DemoteVoter(targetID, 0, 5s) and sleeps 200 ms; the control skips demotion. The case event records the target role, its term before, and the watch parameters. prefix.after: Each case calls MakeClusterCustom with four bootstrapped voters, waits for c.Leader(), selects the first non-leader raft as target, and reads target.GetConfiguration() to record whether the target itself sees its suffrage as voter, nonvoter, absent or unknown. responsibility.before: The library documents that a leadership transfer makes the target up to date, sends TimeoutNow, and that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. Choosing which targets are admissible, and reporting an outcome that matches what happened to authority, are therefore library responsibilities: the caller supplies a member id that the configuration itself currently marks as a non-voter.
responsibility.after: The library owns target eligibility: it holds the latest configuration, its automatic path already excludes non-voters, and its documentation states that a follower which cannot be promoted will fail gracefully. A caller naming a configured member therefore relies on the library either to refuse an ineligible target or to report an outcome that matches what happened to authority.

experiments.revision_reason: Result events now also record candidate_samples and leaderless_samples sampled from each member's State(), and case events record target_role_in_own_config read from the target's own GetConfiguration future; the cluster-wide c.Leader() probe is no longer used inside the sampling loop, which raises the effective sample rate from about one per 116 ms to about one per 10 ms.

scope.description: One follower of a three-voter configuration is driven through real AppendEntries RPCs on its transport while a single heartbeat is executed on a separate goroutine, as the fast-path contract permits. A stable store holds the heartbeat's term write until the main thread has persisted the newer term; the run records the persisted term sequence, the node's current term before and after, and the log and FSM contents at the affected indexes after a stale-leader request.
assumptions: The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered processHeartbeat handler on a separate goroutine, which is what NetworkTransport's connection handler does; the in-memory transport ignores the registration, so the transport's own dispatch is not exercised.
The stable store delays, but never corrupts or fails, one currentTerm write, modelling a slow store write that completes after a newer term has been persisted.

The term 2 and term 4 AppendEntries requests are supplied by the harness to represent a leader that has committed those indexes elsewhere; their commit indexes are asserted by the request, not produced by a quorum of real nodes.
Election and lease timeouts are raised to 30 s so the follower does not campaign during the sequence.
excluded: No attempt to measure how often the interleaving occurs in a real deployment; the probe only establishes that the interleaving is reachable when a store write is delayed.
No real partition or multi-node cluster is used, and the stale leader's authority is modelled by crafted requests.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 blocks one chosen currentTerm value, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. It first commits entries 2 and 3 at term 2 through trans.AppendEntries on the real consumer path, then installs the blocking hook for term 3 and starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying term 3. Once the hook reports that the term 3 write is in flight, the harness sends a term 4 AppendEntries with entry 4 and leader commit 4 through the transport, waits for it to apply, then releases the term 3 write. It records the current term before and after the release, the persisted term and the sequence of term writes, and finally sends the stale term 3 leader's AppendEntries carrying conflicting entries 4 and 5 with leader commit 5, recording whether that request was accepted, the log payloads at indexes 4 and 5, the FSM payloads at those indexes, the applied and commit indexes, and whether the applied payload at index 4 differs from the log payload there.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease and its applied log prefix never to be replaced. The library owns both: it persists the term, it decides when to raise it, and it performs the truncation that can remove an entry. A transport contract that permits concurrent heartbeat delivery does not relax those duties, so the library must make the term update safe against the concurrency it authorises.

comparisons.description: The persisted current term must not fall below a term the node already adopted; a true value contradicts it.
After the regression, the stale leader's conflicting entries must not replace an entry already applied at a higher term; a true value contradicts it.

scope.description: Two hundred attempts per case on a single follower of a three-voter configuration. Each attempt reads the node's current term, starts a fast-path heartbeat carrying that term plus one on its own goroutine, concurrently sends an AppendEntries carrying the term plus two (with one entry and a matching previous-log index) through the real consumer path, waits for both, and counts the attempt as an inversion when the node's term afterwards is below the higher request's term. The first case leaves the stable store undelayed; the second adds a uniform 0-2 ms delay to every current-term write.
assumptions: One node runs; the two peers are addresses only, so each attempt's higher-term request is a supplied leader message rather than a real election outcome.
The heartbeat is delivered by invoking the registered handler on its own goroutine, matching the classification and direct invocation that NetworkTransport performs for this request shape.
The undelayed case is not a control for absence of the defect; it measures how often the race occurs when the store adds no latency of its own.
Attempts run sequentially on the same node and reuse its log; terms advance across attempts and are re-read each time.
excluded: No consequence measurement here: this execution only counts term inversions; the truncation consequence was measured separately in the forced-ordering execution.
No multi-node cluster, no real transport framing and no concurrent client load.

basis.prefix: The harness builds an in-memory stable/log store whose SetUint64 optionally sleeps a uniformly random interval up to a configured maximum before persisting the current term, bootstraps a three-voter configuration containing the local node, and starts NewRaft with 30 s election and lease timeouts so the node stays a follower. For each attempt it reads r.CurrentTerm() and r.LastIndex(), starts r.processHeartbeat on a goroutine with a heartbeat carrying current+1, sends an AppendEntries carrying current+2, the last log index as PrevLogEntry with its stored term, one entry at the next index and leader commit at that index, then waits for both to finish and records whether the current term is below current+2. Each case emits a case event with the attempt count and maximum delay and a result event with the inversion count.
basis.responsibility: Raft requires a server's persisted current term never to decrease. The library owns the term update and it authorises concurrent heartbeat execution through the transport contract, so the update must remain correct under the concurrency it permits regardless of how the store is timed.

comparisons.description: With no added store delay, no attempt may end below the term the main thread persisted.

scope.description: Two restarts of a follower from a real three-voter in-memory cluster with commit-tracking and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled. The leader commits 8400 commands; the chosen follower accumulates them and its own staged commit index is polled until it exceeds 8200. In the control case that follower additionally takes a snapshot before shutdown; in the trigger case it does not. The cluster is then stopped and only the follower is restarted from its retained stores with a fresh transport, bounded by a five-second observation.
assumptions: All three members run the captured code with inmemConfig timeouts and the in-memory commit-tracking store.
The follower's staged commit index is read from its own log store and is therefore what restoreFromCommittedLogs would consume on restart.
The control's snapshot is taken through the follower's own Snapshot future, so the replay it removes is bounded by that follower's applied state.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine; a case that does not return within five seconds is reported as returned=false rather than failing the harness.
excluded: No leader restart, no snapshot shipped from another node, and no client traffic during the restart.
No claim about the exact snapshot index chosen by the follower's snapshot machinery beyond what the case event records.

basis.prefix: Each case builds a three-voter cluster through makeCluster with CommitTrackingLogs and RestoreCommittedLogs, waits for a leader, applies 8400 commands through the leader, and polls the chosen follower's own commit index until it exceeds 8200. In the control it then takes a snapshot on that follower; both cases read the follower's last snapshot index, staged commit index and last log index, shut down the follower and the remaining members, and emit a case event with those values plus the derived replay entries and batches. The harness then calls NewRaft on the follower's retained log, stable and snapshot stores with a fresh transport and a logger-free copy of its config, bounded by five seconds, and emits the returned flag, elapsed time and error.
basis.responsibility: The library owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel and the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so a follower restarting with a legal committed prefix must complete.

comparisons.description: A follower restart whose snapshot bounds the replay must let NewRaft complete.
A follower restart replaying its own committed prefix without a snapshot must let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

scope.description: Two VerifyLeader invocations on real five-member in-memory clusters. Both bootstrap five voters, demote two non-leader members to non-voters, and disconnect the leader's transport from the two remaining voters in both directions. The trigger leaves the two non-voters reachable; the control also disconnects them. Each case records the reachable member counts, the voter quorum, whether the verification completed and with what error, and the leader state afterwards.
assumptions: All members run the captured code on the in-memory transport with one-second heartbeat, election and lease timeouts so the leader is not stepped down by the lease check during the short window.
Disconnect removes routing in both directions, modelling a partition that isolates the leader from those members only.
The verification is bounded by a two-second wait; a verification that never completes is reported as completed=false rather than failing the harness.
The demotions are committed through the leader before the partition; the harness does not separately assert each member's view of the new configuration.
excluded: No claim about read serializability beyond what VerifyLeader itself promises; the harness does not issue reads.
No transfer or configuration change during the partition, and no client traffic.

basis.prefix: Each case builds a five-voter in-memory cluster through MakeClusterCustom with one-second heartbeat, election and lease timeouts, waits for a leader, demotes two non-leader members with DemoteVoter, and sleeps 300 ms. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the two remaining voters in both directions and, in the control only, from the two non-voters as well. The case event records member counts and the voter quorum; the harness calls leader.VerifyLeader(), waits up to two seconds for the future, and emits whether it completed, whether it returned nil, its error text and the leader's state afterwards.

The quorum it sizes is a voter quorum, and the messages it counts must therefore be voter acknowledgements; a non-voter cannot contribute to leadership legitimacy.

scope.description: One two-voter cluster of real nodes over in-memory transports. The harness records the configuration index the leader holds afterwards against its last stored log index, then waits for the node to lead again and applies one client command, comparing the resulting commit index with the other voter's last log index.

basis.prefix: Per case the harness creates an InmemCommitTrackingStore (and InmemSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, assuranceFSM) and emits startup_case_<case> with the configured MaxAppendEntries, staged commit index, last log index, snapshot index and derived replay batch count. Seeded cases store LogCommand entries 1..N and stage commit index N; control_same_entries_larger_batches seeds the same 8193 entries as trigger_129_batches but builds its Config with MaxAppendEntries=1024. Real-prefix cases call BootstrapCluster for a single voter, start the producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, wait for leadership, apply 8300 commands through Apply futures on the leader, optionally call Snapshot(), then Shutdown(). The restart then calls NewRaft with a fresh Config (RestoreCommittedLogs=true), a fresh FSM and a fresh transport on the retained stores, bounded by the case timeout; startup_result_<case> records returned, elapsed_ms, error, sampled FSM apply count and the number of newly blocked processLogs/restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutines relative to a pre-case stack sample. The two added cases seed 131072 and 131073 committed command entries and restart with MaxAppendEntries=1024; their case events record the derived batch count and the result events record whether NewRaft returned.
basis.responsibility: The library, not the caller, owns the size and lifetime of its FSM dispatch channel: it chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs on disk before completing NewRaft, so it must complete for a legal (store, commit index) state rather than block the caller that cannot yet shut it down.

scope.description: Five real nodes over fully connected in-memory transports, bootstrapped from one configuration containing voters A, B and C and non-voters D and E. All nodes share a one-second heartbeat and leader lease; the voters' election timeouts are staggered (A 1.1 s, B 2 s, C and the non-voters 3 s) so that after a partition the two remaining voters do not campaign in lockstep and split the vote. The leader commits 'v1' through a recording FSM, is then disconnected from the other two voters in both directions, and keeps the non-voters reachable in the trigger and loses them in the control. Immediately after the cut the old leader is asked to verify itself; then the harness waits up to twelve seconds for one of the other voters to lead, applies 'v2' there, and asks the old leader to verify itself again before reading its state machine.
assumptions: A caller that verifies the leader before answering a read is the harm model: the experiment measures whether the verification can succeed after the cluster has a different leader.
The injected partition is a bidirectional route removal on the in-memory transports; both sides keep running.
The old leader's lease, not the harness, decides when it stops being leader; the harness only records how that timing compares with the election of a successor.

basis.prefix: The harness creates five in-memory transports and connects every pair in both directions, bootstraps the same configuration (voters A, B, C; non-voters D, E) on all five stores, and starts five rafts each with its own recording FSM. It waits up to ten seconds for a leader, applies 'v1' with a three-second timeout, and sleeps 300 ms so the value is applied everywhere. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the other voters' addresses and theirs from the leader's, and in the control case does the same for the non-voters. It emits sr_case_<case> with the leader identity, the reachable voter and non-voter counts, the initial value and the leader's FSM value, records the cut time, calls VerifyLeader with a two-second bound and records whether it completed, whether it succeeded, its error and the milliseconds since the cut. It waits up to twelve seconds for a voter other than the old leader to report Leader, applies 'v2' there with a three-second timeout, sleeps 300 ms, and records the successor's identity, apply result, FSM value and the milliseconds since the cut. It then calls VerifyLeader on the old leader again with a two-second bound and reads the old leader's FSM value before healing the partition. It emits sr_result_<case> with all of those fields plus stale_verified_read, which is true only when the post-failover verification succeeded and the old leader's value differs from the successor's committed value.
basis.responsibility: VerifyLeader is the licence a caller uses before serving a local read: success tells the caller this node is still the leader that a fresh read requires. If that licence can be issued while fewer voters than the voter quorum can answer, the licence is issued on support the configuration does not count, and the caller's read is only as fresh as the moment the real quorum moved on. The experiment measures whether that window exists in practice and how it compares with the time a successor needs.

On return it shuts the node down; on timeout it records that no return was observed and leaves the node alone, since the *Raft was never handed back. It emits rb_result_<case> with returned, elapsed_ms, error, the FSM's applied count sampled after the observation, and the change in the number of goroutines whose stack contains processLogs. basis.responsibility: Starting a node from already-committed entries is a startup path the library offers, and it must either complete or report an error. A constructor that blocks because it produced into a channel whose only consumer it has not started yet cannot do either: the caller never receives the node, so the caller has no way to start, serve or shut it down. The experiment measures the exact entry count at which that happens at the smallest legal batch size, which tests the stated product rather than a single configuration.

comparisons.description: Exactly 128 batches, one entry each, is within the channel capacity and must let the constructor return.
One entry past the boundary must still let the constructor return; the harness records that it does not.
A completed replay would leave all 129 replayed entries applied to the state machine.

semantic_changes: The prefix now takes its snapshot between two batches of commands instead of after all of them, so the replay is shortened rather than eliminated.
The short case's replay is four batches, which is the region earlier receipts left inferred.
Every result event records the snapshot index, staged commit index and replay arithmetic so the gap can be recomputed from the receipt.

scope.description: A real single-node cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled commits a first batch of commands, takes a snapshot, commits a second batch, and shuts down. Both stores are retained, so the restart's replay is the difference between the staged commit index and the snapshot index. The short case uses 200 then 200 commands, which leaves a gap of roughly 198 entries or four FSM batches at MaxAppendEntries=64; the long case uses 200 then 8300, which leaves about 8300 entries or 130 batches. Each restart is started on a separate goroutine and bounded, and the events record the snapshot index, staged commit index, last log index, replay entries and batches, whether NewRaft returned, the elapsed time, the error and the number of goroutines left in processLogs.
assumptions: The snapshot taken between the two batches is durable in the in-memory snapshot store and is the newest snapshot on restart, so the replay starts after it.
The leader stages a commit index at the pre-dispatch index, so the staged commit index is the entry count rather than the last log index; the harness reports both so the gap can be recomputed.
A constructor that has not returned within the five-second window is treated as having made no progress.
excluded: No multi-node cluster and no snapshot taken during the replay.
Only MaxAppendEntries=64, the default; the boundary was sampled at other batch sizes by earlier receipts.
No attempt to shut down a node whose constructor never returned.

basis.prefix: The harness bootstraps a single-voter configuration, starts one raft with 50 ms timeouts and RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, waits up to ten seconds for leadership, applies the first batch of commands with five-second futures, calls Snapshot(), applies the second batch, reads the newest snapshot index from the snapshot store, reads the staged commit index and last log index from the log store, and shuts the node down. It then computes the replay as the staged commit index minus the snapshot index and the batch count as ceil(replay/MaxAppendEntries) and emits rc_case_<case> with the mode, the option flag, the batch sizes, the snapshot index, the staged commit index, the last log index, the replay entries and batches and the observation timeout. It then starts NewRaft on a fresh transport over the retained stores in a goroutine and waits up to the configured timeout. On return it shuts the node down; on timeout it records that no return was observed and leaves the node alone. It emits rc_result_<case> with the same identifiers, the batch parameters, returned, elapsed_ms, error and the change in the number of goroutines whose stack contains processLogs.
basis.responsibility: Restarting from a snapshot plus a tail of committed entries is the normal recovery path for this option, and the library must complete it whenever the tail fits within the replay's dispatch capacity. The experiment measures that path with a real prefix rather than a seeded store, so the recovery region between a zero-length replay and a blocked one is observed instead of inferred.

comparisons.description: A real restart whose snapshot leaves a short tail must let NewRaft return.
The short case must actually replay a non-zero tail, so that it exercises the shortened-replay region rather than the zero-replay control.
The same recovery path with a tail past 128 batches must still let NewRaft return; the harness records that it does not.

semantic_changes: The delay becomes a swept parameter with five settings instead of one trigger value plus a zero-delay control.
Each case builds its own store, transport and raft, so the delay distribution cannot carry over between settings.
Events report the maximum delay in microseconds alongside the inversion count, so the curve can be read from the receipt.

scope.description: One follower node in a three-voter configuration that no live peer drives, with a stable store that optionally sleeps for a uniform random interval before persisting the current term. For each of five delay settings the harness runs 200 attempts; each attempt issues one fast-path heartbeat carrying cur+1 on its own goroutine while a term cur+2 AppendEntries with one entry goes through the real consumer path, then waits for both and records whether the node's current term ended below cur+2. Delay settings are 0, 250 us, 500 us, 1 ms and 2 ms of maximum delay per current-term write.
assumptions: The heartbeat shape used here is the one NetworkTransport classifies as a fast path: non-zero term, a leader address, zero previous-log fields, no entries and zero leader commit index.
The delay is applied only to the current-term key, so other stable writes are unaffected and the comparison isolates the term write.
The term cur+2 request reaches the node through the transport's consumer path, which is how a non-heartbeat AppendEntries arrives.
An attempt counts as an inversion when the node's term after both operations is below the higher term it was sent.
excluded: No real leader, partition or quorum; the requests are crafted and their commit indexes are asserted by the request.
No disk-backed store: the delay is a sleep before an in-memory write.
No sweep above 2 ms and no per-request distribution other than uniform from zero.

basis.prefix: For each case the harness creates a fresh in-memory stable store wrapped so that a write to the current-term key sleeps for a uniform random duration below the case's maximum, a fresh in-memory transport, and one raft with 30 s timeouts, three voters (the local node plus two addresses with no process) and the option defaults. It bootstraps the configuration, then repeats the attempt 200 times: read the current term and last index, start the fast-path heartbeat on a goroutine through processHeartbeat with a term one above current, build a term-two-above AppendEntries carrying one entry at the last index and a matching previous-log term, send it through the transport, wait for the heartbeat, and count an inversion when the node's term afterwards is below the higher term. Between attempts it sleeps one millisecond. Each case emits sw_case_<case> with the attempt count and the maximum delay in microseconds, and sw_result_<case> with the same fields plus inversion_count.
basis.responsibility: The library permits the registered heartbeat handler to run concurrently with the main AppendEntries path, and it advertises that concurrency as a way to avoid inflating election timeouts for disk latency. The term update must therefore remain monotonic across that overlap, not only when the stable store is instantaneous; the sweep measures how much store latency the current code tolerates before the race saturates.

comparisons.description: With no added delay, the same race must not leave the node below the higher term in any attempt.
A maximum current-term delay of 250 us must not be enough to lose the race.
A maximum current-term delay of 500 us must not be enough to lose the race.
A maximum current-term delay of 1 ms must not be enough to lose the race.
A maximum current-term delay of 2 ms must not be enough to lose the race; this is the setting the earlier two-point probe used.

semantic_changes: The cluster has four members and one non-voter instead of five members and two non-voters.
The harness records whether the demoted member's own configuration converged before the partition, so the case cannot be explained by a stale view on the acknowledging node.
Case and result events use a new prefix so they cannot be confused with the earlier five-member receipts.

scope.description: Four real members over the cluster helper's in-memory transports, bootstrapped from one four-voter configuration; one non-leader member is demoted with DemoteVoter and the harness waits until that member's own configuration view no longer lists it as a voter. The leader is then disconnected in both directions from the two other voters and, in the trigger, left connected to the single non-voter; the control also disconnects the non-voter. Each case records the reachable voter and non-voter counts, the voter quorum, whether the demotion converged, and the bounded VerifyLeader result with the node's state afterwards.
assumptions: Bidirectional route removal on the in-memory transports models a partition; no process is stopped.
The demoted member's own view is the check that the configuration change reached the node whose acknowledgement is being counted.
A verification that has not completed within two seconds is recorded as incomplete rather than as a success or failure.
excluded: No client read and no second suffrage shape beyond one non-voter.
No demotion of the sitting leader and no cluster larger than four members.
No variation of the lease timeout.

basis.prefix: The harness bootstraps four voters, picks the leader and the three other members, demotes the first non-leader member, and polls that member's GetConfiguration until it no longer reports itself as a voter or two seconds pass, recording whether it converged and after how long. It then disconnects the leader's transport from the other two voters' addresses and theirs from the leader's, and in the control case does the same for the non-voter. It emits vx_case_<case> with the membership counts, the reachable counts, the voter quorum and the demotion convergence, calls VerifyLeader with a two-second bound, and emits vx_result_<case> with whether the call completed, whether it succeeded, its error, the elapsed milliseconds and the node's state afterwards.
basis.responsibility: VerifyLeader sizes its quorum from the voter count, so a leader that can reach only itself among the voters has one of the two acknowledgements its own sizing requires. The experiment asks whether a single non-voter, rather than a particular larger suffrage mix, is enough to supply the missing acknowledgement and let the call report success.

comparisons.description: With one of three voters reachable, a verification sized on the voter quorum must fail; the harness records whether a single non-voter changes that.
Control: with the non-voter unreachable too, no supporter remains and the verification must fail.

semantic_changes: The transfer is issued concurrently with the demotion instead of after it converges.
Each attempt uses a fresh cluster, which is required because the demotion changes the configuration permanently.
The result is summarised across 20 attempts rather than reported per case, and includes how many attempts ended with the target as a non-voter.

scope.description: Twenty independent attempts, each on a fresh four-voter in-memory cluster. Per attempt the harness picks the leader and one follower, starts DemoteVoter for that follower on a goroutine, then immediately calls LeadershipTransferToServer for the same member on whichever node is leader at that moment, both with bounded waits. It records whether each future succeeded, whether the target ever reported Leader during the following two seconds, which member led at the end, and the target's own suffrage at the end.
assumptions: Starting the demotion and issuing the transfer without an intervening wait is the tightest race the public API allows; the caller cannot observe commit state between the two calls without waiting.
The target is chosen at demotion time from the members that are not leading, so the demotion never targets the sitting leader.
An attempt in which the target reports Leader at any sample counts as an elevation even if it later steps down.
excluded: No repeated demotions on one cluster; a fresh cluster is built per attempt because a member can be demoted only once.
No partition, no restart, and no client traffic during the race.
The transfer target's address is read before the demotion, so a member whose address changed as part of the demotion is out of scope.

basis.prefix: The harness bootstraps a four-voter cluster through the cluster helper, reads the leader and the first non-leader member, records the target's identifier and address, starts DemoteVoter(target, 5s) on a goroutine, re-reads the leader, and immediately starts LeadershipTransferToServer(target, address) on a goroutine as well. It waits up to five seconds for the demotion future and up to three for the transfer future, recording both results. It then samples the target's State every 10 ms for two seconds, recording whether the target ever reports Leader, reads the cluster's leader at the end, and reads the target's own configuration to record its final suffrage. After all attempts it emits cv_result_demotion_race with the attempt count, how many demotions succeeded, how many transfers succeeded, how many attempts saw the target lead, how many ended with the target leading, how many ended with the target as a non-voter, and the last transfer error.
basis.responsibility: A transfer must not install a member as leader while the configuration that removes its vote is in flight. The public API offers no way to make the demotion and the transfer atomic, so the question is whether the ordering the library itself imposes, with voters rejecting a candidate their applied configuration no longer counts, is enough to prevent the elevation when the two requests are issued back to back.

comparisons.description: A member whose vote is being removed must not become leader in any attempt, even when the transfer races the demotion.
No attempt may end with the demoted member leading.
All twenty transfer futures are expected to complete without error, which is what makes the absence of elevation a silent failure rather than a reported one.

semantic_changes: The trigger window grows from five seconds to thirty seconds while the state under test stays the boundary pair already used at the default batch size.
The control gets its own longer window, so the comparison is between a completed replay and a blocked one rather than between two five-second cutoffs.
Events are split into a case event before the attempt and a result event after it, so the admission record is separate from the outcome.

scope.description: Two cases on an in-memory commit-tracking store with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the default MaxAppendEntries of 64: 8192 seeded entries, which is exactly 128 batches, watched for ten seconds, and 8193 entries, which is 129 batches, watched for thirty seconds. Each case starts NewRaft on a separate goroutine because a caller that observes no return cannot call Shutdown, and records whether the constructor returned, how long the observation lasted, the error, and whether a new goroutine was left inside processLogs.
assumptions: The control's completion time in this harness, a few milliseconds, is representative of how long a replay of 128 batches takes here, so a thirty-second window is thousands of times longer than a completed replay needs.
A constructor that has not returned within the window is treated as having made no progress; the harness does not claim to prove an infinite block, only that thirty seconds is not enough.
The seeded entries are ordinary command entries at term 1 with the staged commit index equal to the entry count and no snapshot.
excluded: No real cluster and no snapshot.
Only one longer window; the effect of the crash-recovery timeout between NewRaft and the caller is not exercised.
No attempt to interrupt or shut down the blocked node.

basis.prefix: For each case the harness seeds an InmemCommitTrackingStore with the entry count, stages the commit index to that count, and emits pp_case_<case> with the entries, the computed batch count, the batch size, the window length and the option flag. It then starts NewRaft on a goroutine with a fresh in-memory transport, a recording FSM and the default configuration plus RestoreCommittedLogs, and waits up to the case's window. On return it shuts the node down; on timeout it records that no return was observed and leaves the node alone. It emits pp_result_<case> with returned, elapsed_ms, error and the change in the number of goroutines whose stack contains processLogs.
basis.responsibility: A constructor that has not returned within a window thousands of times longer than a completed replay of the same shape needs is not merely slow; the caller cannot start, serve or shut the node down. The experiment measures whether the blocked case ever completes on a timescale far beyond the control's completion time.

comparisons.description: The 128-batch control must let the constructor return well inside its window.
One entry past the same boundary must still let the constructor return within thirty seconds; the harness records that it does not.

semantic_changes: The current-term write now performs a real file write and fsync instead of sleeping for a random interval.
The result event reports the measured mean and maximum write latency and the number of term writes, so the exercised latency is inspectable.
There is one case only; the earlier jitter receipts remain the low-latency control.

scope.description: One follower node in a three-voter configuration that no live peer drives, with a stable store that writes the eight bytes of the current term to a real file and calls fsync before updating the in-memory value. Two hundred attempts each issue one fast-path heartbeat carrying cur+1 on its own goroutine while a term cur+2 AppendEntries with one entry goes through the transport's consumer path; an attempt counts as an inversion when the node's term afterwards is below the higher term it was sent. The harness records the inversion count, the number of term writes, and the mean and maximum duration of the file write plus fsync.
assumptions: The file write and fsync happen before the in-memory stable value is updated, mirroring a store that persists before acknowledging, so the latency sits in the same place as the synthetic delay it replaces.
The measured latency is a property of this container's filesystem; the mean and maximum are recorded so the receipt shows what was actually exercised.
The heartbeat shape and the term-two-above AppendEntries are the same as in the jitter experiments, so the cases differ only in what makes the term write slow.
excluded: No synthetic delay at all: the only latency is the filesystem's.
No real leader, partition or quorum; the requests remain crafted.
No control without any write latency, which the earlier jitter receipts already supply.

parameters.store: file write plus fsync per current-term update

basis.prefix: The harness creates a temporary directory, opens a term file in it, and wraps an in-memory stable store so that a write to the current-term key encodes the value, writes it at offset zero, calls Sync, and only then forwards to the in-memory store while recording the duration. It bootstraps a three-voter configuration with 30 s timeouts, starts one raft, and repeats the attempt 200 times: read the current term and last index, start the fast-path heartbeat on a goroutine through processHeartbeat with a term one above current, send a term-two-above AppendEntries carrying one entry through the transport, wait for the heartbeat, and count an inversion when the node's term is afterwards below the higher term. Between attempts it sleeps one millisecond. It emits cd_case_fsync_term_writes before the loop and cd_result_fsync_term_writes afterwards with the inversion count, the number of term writes, and the mean and maximum write duration in microseconds.
basis.responsibility: The library accepts concurrent heartbeats specifically so that election timeouts need not cover disk latency, which means the term update must stay monotonic when the stable-store write takes as long as a real fsync. A delay injected by the harness shows the mechanism; a real file write plus fsync shows the exposure under latency the deployment actually has.

comparisons.description: With a real fsync on the current-term write, no attempt may end below the higher term it was sent.

scope.description: Three restarts of retained single-node cluster state with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and MaxAppendEntries at its default of 64: a first batch of two hundred committed commands followed by a snapshot, then a second batch of 3200, 8194 or 8195 commands, so the restart replays only the tail after the snapshot and that tail is about fifty, exactly one hundred and twenty eight, or one hundred and twenty nine FSM batches.
assumptions: The producing raft writes the same commit-tracking store, snapshot store and transport that the restart reads, so the replay state is produced through the normal leader, commit and apply path rather than seeded.
MaxAppendEntries stays at the DefaultConfig value of 64 and fsmMutateCh keeps its captured capacity, so the batch count is the only variable across the last pair.
NewRaft is invoked on its own goroutine and observed for a bounded window; a case that does not return is reported as returned=false rather than as a harness failure.
The snapshot produced by the first batch is at index 202, so the tail size is the second batch plus the two committed entries the first batch leaves beyond the snapshot.
excluded: No assertions about commit safety, voting or membership; this probe addresses startup progress only.
No variation of the channel capacity, the batch size, or the store implementation; only the tail length changes.
The snapshot is always taken between the two batches; snapshots taken during a running second batch are not exercised.

basis.prefix: Each case bootstraps a single-voter Configuration and starts a producing raft with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, InmemCommitTrackingStore as both log and stable store, an InmemSnapshotStore, an InmemTransport on the same address the restart will use, and an FSM that counts applied entries. The producing raft waits for leadership, applies the first batch of 200 commands through Apply futures, calls Snapshot(), applies the second batch, records the listed snapshot index, then Shutdown(). The case event emits the snapshot index, the store's staged commit index, the last log index, the derived replay entry count and batch count, the batch size and the observation window. The restart then constructs a fresh Config, FSM and transport over the retained stores on its own goroutine, records the number of goroutines parked inside processLogs before it starts, and waits up to the window for the constructor; the result event emits returned, elapsed_ms, error and the change in the parked-goroutine count.
basis.responsibility: The library chooses the batch size, creates fsmMutateCh with a fixed capacity, and decides the order in which NewRaft starts the FSM consumer, so a replay whose batch count exceeds that capacity blocks inside its own constructor. The documented RestoreCommittedLogs option promises to replay all known-committed logs before completing NewRaft, and the caller receives no handle to shut down until the constructor returns, so the replay must complete for any legal tail rather than only for tails shorter than the channel.

comparisons.description: A real prefix whose snapshot leaves about fifty replay batches must let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
A real prefix replaying 8192 entries, exactly the 128 batches the channel holds, must let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.
One committed entry beyond the capacity, on the same real prefix shape, must still let NewRaft complete; a false witness contradicts it.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft calls restoreFromCommittedLogs synchronously, which sends commitTuple batches into fsmMutateCh from processLogs, while the only goroutine that reads that channel is started after the constructor returns.

The startup replay can enqueue at most 128 batches because fsmMutateCh holds 128 entries, so with the default MaxAppendEntries of 64 a replay of more than 8192 committed entries has no enabled progress path.

scope.description: Two transfer attempts on separate four-member clusters with one demoted member each: an automatic LeadershipTransfer() control on a cluster whose demoted member is a follower, and an explicit LeadershipTransferToServer for that demoted member on an identical cluster.
assumptions: The demoted member is chosen at the moment of demotion so it is a follower, because demoting the sitting leader starts a transfer of its own.
Each case bootstraps its own cluster, so the two cases share no state.
The harness waits up to two seconds for the demoted member's own GetConfiguration to report the non-voter role before transferring, and records whether that convergence happened.
A transfer future is awaited for at most five seconds per attempt and at most five attempts are made, retrying only while the error names a transfer already in progress.
excluded: No assertion about data safety or about entries applied during the transfer; the probe records the outcome of one client write after the watch window.
The five-member cluster and the non-converged demotion race are covered by other receipts and are not repeated here.
Failover time and vote counts are sampled every ten milliseconds, so an interval shorter than that can be missed.

basis.prefix: Each case bootstraps a four-peer cluster with the in-memory transport and waits for a leader, demotes one non-leader member with DemoteVoter, and polls that member's GetConfiguration until its own view reports the non-voter role. A case event records the mode, the demoted member, its role view, convergence time and the leader before the transfer. The control calls LeadershipTransfer() and the trigger calls LeadershipTransferToServer(targetID, targetAddress); each future is awaited on its own goroutine for at most five seconds, and while the error names a transfer already in progress the harness retries, up to five attempts, recording every attempt's error. A result event records the future outcome, per-attempt errors, whether the target ever reported Leader during a three-second sample, the leaderless sample count, the final leader and whether it is a voter, then submits one client Apply and one GetConfiguration to the current leader and records their errors.
basis.responsibility: LeadershipTransferToServer accepts a caller-named member and is documented as transferring leadership to that server; the library, not the caller, owns the target check and the transfer bookkeeping. On a configuration in which the named member has no vote, the same library already skips such members when it chooses a target itself, so the explicit entry point is the only path that can admit a target that cannot win, and it must either refuse that target or install it.

comparisons.description: The automatic transfer on a cluster that contains a demoted member must complete without error; a false witness contradicts it.
If an explicit transfer to a configured member is admitted rather than refused for having no vote, that member must become leader; a false witness contradicts it.

knowledge.assertion: pickServer skips servers whose suffrage is not Voter, while an explicit id is looked up in leaderState.replState, which contains non-voters, and proceeds to replicate and send TimeoutNow.
A voter receiving a RequestVote from a configured non-voter adopts a higher term and steps down before rejecting the vote, and timeoutNow performs no membership check.

scope.description: Two cases on separate four-member clusters with one demoted follower each: a single explicit transfer to the demoted member with the leader's transfer flag sampled around the call, and the five-attempt retry sequence with the flag sampled before every attempt.
assumptions: The demoted member is a follower at demotion time, chosen as any member other than the sitting leader.
Each case bootstraps its own cluster, so the two cases share no state.
The harness waits up to two seconds for the demoted member's own GetConfiguration to report the non-voter role and records whether it converged.
The transfer flag is read through the package-internal accessor on the node that is leader at the moment of the call, so the sample describes the node the request is sent to.
excluded: No assertion about client-write availability after the transfer; that was measured in the previous receipt.
Only explicit transfers are issued; the automatic form is covered by the earlier control.
Leadership is sampled every ten milliseconds from each member's State, so a shorter leaderless interval can be missed.

basis.prefix: Each case bootstraps a four-peer in-memory cluster, waits for a leader, demotes a non-leader member with DemoteVoter, and polls that member's GetConfiguration until it reports the non-voter role. A case event records the demoted member, its role view, convergence time and the leader before the transfer. The single case samples getLeadershipTransferInProgress on the leader, calls LeadershipTransferToServer once, samples the flag again as soon as the future is returned, awaits the future for at most five seconds, samples the flag after completion and again after three hundred milliseconds. The retry case reproduces the five-attempt loop, sampling the flag before each attempt and recording each attempt's error, retrying only while the error names a transfer already in progress. Both result events record the future outcome, the flag samples, whether the named member ever reported Leader during a three-second sample, the leaderless sample count and the final leader.
basis.responsibility: LeadershipTransferToServer accepts a caller-named member and is documented as transferring leadership to that server; the library owns both the target check and the bookkeeping that decides whether a transfer is already running. An in-progress error returned for a request that was issued while no transfer was running would attribute the failure to that request, while one returned because an earlier transfer was still active would mean the named target was never attempted at all.

comparisons.description: A single explicit transfer to a configured member must install that member if it is accepted; a false witness contradicts it.

The first request must be issued while no transfer is running, so that any in-progress error belongs to that request rather than to an earlier one; a true witness would instead explain the earlier receipt as a prior stalled transfer.

knowledge.assertion: An explicit transfer target is resolved only through leaderState.replState, which includes non-voters, while pickServer skips non-voters.
A voter adopts a higher term and steps down before rejecting a configured non-voter candidate, and timeoutNow forces candidacy without checking suffrage or term.
